narrative_purpose: A label-ready spatial cutaway turns the Eastern Sea from a flat horizon into connected lagoon, reef, slope, water-column and deep habitats.
subject: A single continuous side cutaway through an alien ocean island: a shallow sheltered lagoon with arching root-like marine plants at far right, a low living reef crest breaking waves, a steep outer reef wall descending leftward, and a vast open water column grading into darkness. One small blue-skinned diver crosses the upper slope. Sparse fish occupy the surface, while faint marine particles appear below.
scene: An idealized naturalist transect across an Awa'atlu-like atoll and the adjacent Eastern Sea, with the water shown transparent enough to read the underwater relief.
camera: Wide straight-on sectional landscape, horizon high in frame, lagoon at right and deep sea at left, with no exploded panels.
light: Cyan daylight illuminates the lagoon and reef crest, angled shafts weaken across the slope, and deep water shifts to indigo with subtle teal life glows.
palette: Cyan and living teal in the upper reef, muted stone substrate, ocean-teal middle water and void-indigo depth with minimal magenta accents.
style: Painterly naturalist field plate with credible spatial continuity, not a vector diagram.
detail_level: Clear reef crest, lagoon roots, outer slope and depth transition; simple open water and dark margins reserved framed by deep negative space.
composition: Four legible zones arranged right to left and top to bottom: lagoon, reef rim, descending wall and deep reservoir. Keep open dark space beside each zone framed by deep negative space.
consistency_notes: Match the atoll, diver and marine palette established by fig-00-cover. Maintain one continuous ocean rather than a collage.
negative_prompt: no text, no lettering, no labels, no arrows, no map symbols, no infographic chrome, no photographic or 3D-render look, no split-screen collage
